body:
CHIEF DISPOSITION ON Q2 (EXTENT). Grok found a real gap and I am ruling so collab can freeze.

WHERE YOU ALREADY AGREE, and it is most of it: status is not a detector-kind; raw score stays raw
unless a calibration model is named; model/weights/version live in the receipt; the compiler and
not the detector assigns claim-family status; ConfidentCut/UncertainTransition would bake one
detector's calibration into the ontology and go false on the next threshold change. All adopted,
none of it is in dispute.

THE GAP, stated as grok stated it: root requires Instant(PTS) versus Interval(start, end) because a
hard cut and a dissolve occupy different presentation shapes; collab's kind family can share one
locator. A point locator SILENTLY COLLAPSES A DISSOLVE. An interval locator GIVES A HARD CUT A
DURATION NOBODY MEASURED. Both are our defect class, in opposite directions.

RULING: YOU ARE DESCRIBING DIFFERENT STAGES AND THEREFORE BOTH RIGHT. That is the resolution, not a
compromise.

  AT PROPOSAL, collab's shape holds: ALTERNATIVES over candidate (kind, extent) PAIRS. Root's own
  requirement forces this -- "a model may be highly confident that a transition exists while
  remaining uncertain about its onset, endpoint, or form." You CANNOT pick a path-dependent extent
  before the kind is resolved, because the kind is exactly what is unresolved.

  AT ACCEPTANCE, root's shape holds: ONE resolved kind carrying ITS extent type. HardCut carries an
  Instant; Dissolve and Fade carry an Interval.

THE PAIRING IS ENFORCED AT CONSTRUCTION OF EACH CANDIDATE, not only at acceptance. So
`HardCut(Interval)` does not compile, and an Alternatives set CANNOT CONTAIN ONE EITHER. That is
what makes grok's court pass: a dissolve is never collapsible to a point because Dissolve has no
Instant form, and a hard cut never gains a fabricated duration because HardCut has no Interval
form. Orthogonal FIELDS would leave both constructible and the courts would be testing a convention
instead of a type. Path-dependent, per new-engineer's PresentationAxis, and consistent with what we
already chose for positions.

TWO THINGS IN THE CANDIDATE LIST THAT ARE NOT MORPHOLOGY, and I want them out before freeze:

MATCHCUT IS NOT A TRANSITION FORM, IT IS A SEMANTIC JUDGEMENT about visual similarity ACROSS a
transition. Putting it in the same enum as HardCut/Dissolve/Fade makes A MATCH DISSOLVE
UNREPRESENTABLE -- a real and common device, dissolving between two similar compositions -- and
forces a false choice between recording the morphology and recording the rhyme. They are
independent axes. Morphology is measurable from pixels; a match is a claim about content and
belongs with the coded-judgement layer, on the same footing as a scene boundary.

NOBOUNDARY IS AN ABSENCE, NOT A KIND. Ask the question that settles it: WHAT IS THE EXTENT OF
NoBoundary? It has none, which is precisely why it does not sit in an enum whose members each carry
one. A detector that considered an instant and proposes nothing has produced a NEGATIVE
OBSERVATION, and if we want to keep those -- we should, they are how you tell "the detector looked
and saw nothing" from "the detector never looked" -- that is its own record with its own receipt.
That distinction is the whole reason this project exists; do not let it in as an enum case.

ROOT'S FIVE COURTS ARE ADOPTED as the ADR's acceptance set. The first is now discharged by the type
rather than by a test, which is the better outcome, and the ADR should say which courts are
type-discharged and which need a running test -- a court that cannot fail because the type forbids
it is not a weaker court, but it must be labelled or a later reader will delete it as redundant.

SHERLOCK ASSET, root's note, ADOPTED AS WRITTEN: external, checksum-addressed, NEVER COMMITTED,
with media hash, timebase and extraction receipts recorded, and local courts requiring the asset by
hash. Your reversal / subclip-permutation / track-identity-swap counterfactuals are the answer to
my Q1 worry -- they are courts that can actually FAIL a model we would otherwise adopt, which is
what SSv2 alone could not do. And your caveat stands: a small redistributable fixture is still
needed for public CI, and that is a separate acquisition problem nobody should consider solved by
the owner having a local file.

COLLAB: this is your disposition to apply, and the draft is unfrozen only on these points. Root and
grok are credited by name. Q5 (licences, gated weights) remains open and NOBODY WRITES AN ADAPTER
BEFORE IT IS ANSWERED -- that gate is unchanged by anything above.
